title: Resolution cancellation for the specified point comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$, with its constant $\mathcal O_E$-action, on the small pro-etale site in its module universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For any flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], set $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_{P,n}(x)=x\otimes1$ and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Put $C(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$ with the actual coefficient-induced transitions $v_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), and $D(P)_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B(P)_n=\Gamma C(P)_n$. All towers are restricted to the single integral coefficient ring. For any strict tower $X$ with transitions $w_n$ put $s_X((x_n))=(w_nx_{n+1})$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For a strict tower map $f:X\to Y$ let $H(f)(b,a)=((\prod_nf_n)b,(\prod_nf_n)a)$. Let $c_X:\Gamma H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(\Gamma X)$ be the normalized identity on both sectionwise product coordinates for a tower of $R$-module sheaves [def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison].

Put $\theta_{P,n}=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_{P,n})$ and $\widetilde\theta_P(w)=(0,(\theta_{P,n}w)_n)$ using [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Let $N$ be any complex of $R$-module sheaves and $q:P\to N$ a quasi-isomorphism. Let $Lg^*$ be the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Under its specified resolution comparison let $b_q:\Gamma Lg^*[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}[H(B(P))]$ be obtained by identifying its representative with $H(C(P))$ and then using $c_{C(P)}$. Denote by $\kappa_{N,q}=[\widetilde\theta_P][g^{-1}q]^{-1}$ the integral comparison formed using this resolution, as in comparison (b), and put $\iota_{N,q}=\Gamma(\kappa_{N,q})\sigma_N$, where $\sigma$ is the restriction/colimit-insertion map [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Brackets denote classes in the ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Then $\Gamma(q)$ and $\Gamma(g^{-1}q)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, $\sigma_N\Gamma(q)=\Gamma(g^{-1}q)\sigma_P$, and
$$b_q\iota_{N,q}=[c_{C(P)}\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}.$$
These formulas hold for every such resolution, with the specified representative comparisons, and agree with the defining $\iota_N$ when $q$ is the resolution chosen to define comparison (b). No completeness or constructibility of $N$ is assumed. Only resolution quasi-isomorphisms and the specified comparison isomorphisms are inverted; no augmentation of $\Gamma P$ into its reduction cone is asserted invertible.

source.place: clause (3), point-transport comparison supplement; original steps 4 and 5: naturality of sigma, exactness, specified comparison and resolution cancellation

proof.text: Comparison (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] explicitly makes the transported module inverse image exact, including for the completed ring, and states that it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Apply this to $q$ to obtain that $g^{-1}q$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $R$-module complexes. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], termwise sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms for every ring sheaf on this geometric point. Apply this to $q$ and $g^{-1}q$. Restricting the resulting scalar actions along the constant map $\mathcal O_E\to\Gamma(s,R)$ changes neither kernels, images nor the underlying homology groups, so $\Gamma(q)$ and $\Gamma(g^{-1}q)$ remain quasi-isomorphisms of ordinary $\mathcal O_E$-complexes. This argument applies to unbounded complexes and does not use completeness of $N$.

source.place: Tag 098H, lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible; application via the cited exact-point-sections lemma, together with the explicit completed-module exactness in comparison (b)

proof.text: Use the defining section formula in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]: frobeniusPointIntegralSigma in degree i is restriction along the site arrow (s,g) to (s,id), in the canonical sectionwise inverse-image coordinates. Apply naturality of the module sheaf map q^i to that site arrow. The resulting equality on every section gives the strict sigma square after HomologicalComplex.hom_ext. This works for all complexes and requires no separate general automorphism-transport theorem.

source.place: clause (3), point-transport supplement: restriction and colimit-insertion naturality, original step 4; explicit argument supplied by agent

proof.text: Use the actual coefficient-induced transitions from [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Its formula $v_n\theta_{P,n+1}=\theta_{P,n}$ implies $(1-s_{C(P)})(\theta_{P,n})_n=0$. Hence the prescribed lift is a chain map: $d(0,(\theta_{P,n}w)_n)=(0,(\theta_{P,n}dw)_n)$ for every local section $w$. The normalized comparison of [def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison] acts identically on both sectionwise product coordinates. Thus $e_P=c_{C(P)}\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P$ is a chain map whose degreewise value is $e_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(\theta_{P,n})\sigma_P(z))_n)$. This checks the zero shifted-product component as well as the unshifted component; no replacement of the specified comparison is made.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; signed shifted-cone calculation with the explicitly specified comparison (b)

proof.text: Write $Q=[\Gamma(q)]$ and $T=[\Gamma(g^{-1}q)]$. These are isomorphisms by step 1 and the localization definition of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. After taking classes, step 2 reads $[\sigma_N]Q=T[\sigma_P]$. Compose on the left with $T^{-1}$ and on the right with $Q^{-1}$ to get $T^{-1}[\sigma_N]=[\sigma_P]Q^{-1}$, by associativity and the inverse identities. Also $\Gamma([g^{-1}q]^{-1})=T^{-1}$: applying the sections functor to both inverse identities shows that its image is an inverse of $T$, hence the unique inverse. Thus no additional localization or augmentation inverse is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; elementary inverse and functor calculation in the localized category

proof.text:
Let $j_q:[H(C(P))]\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*[N]$ denote the specified resolution comparison, with this orientation. The definition of $\kappa_{N,q}$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), read under that comparison, says $\kappa_{N,q}=j_q[\widetilde\theta_P][g^{-1}q]^{-1}$. The specified definition of $b_q$ is $[c_{C(P)}]\Gamma(j_q)^{-1}$. Therefore functoriality, cancellation of $\Gamma(j_q)$, and step 4 give
$$b_q\iota_{N,q}=[c_{C(P)}][\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)]T^{-1}[\sigma_N]=[c_{C(P)}\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P]Q^{-1}.$$
The first equality expands $\iota_{N,q}=\Gamma(\kappa_{N,q})[\sigma_N]$ and the second substitutes $T^{-1}[\sigma_N]=[\sigma_P]Q^{-1}$. The chain map inside the last brackets is the explicitly normalized $e_P$ of step 3.

source.place: clause (3), point-transport supplement: specified representative comparison and cancellation, original step 5; elementary composite written out by agent

proof.text: The preceding calculation began with an arbitrary flat-term K-flat $P$ and arbitrary quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to N$ as in the statement. Its only identifications were the specified $j_q$ and $c_{C(P)}$, so it proves the formulas for every such resolution with those comparisons. When $q$ is the resolution chosen in comparison (b), the formula for $\kappa_{N,q}$ is exactly the defining $\kappa_N$. The integral clause of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] defines $\iota_N$ as $\Gamma(\kappa_N)\sigma_N$; hence for that chosen resolution the displayed formula is the formula for the defining $\iota_N$. For an arbitrary $N$ it gives the asserted recipe $\iota_{N,q}$ without claiming that $N$ belongs to the constructible subcategory on which the fibre functor is named. The only inverted maps were resolution quasi-isomorphisms and specified comparison isomorphisms.
